messages:
Ravi: hey team, quick QA: trying to onboard a customer with the ruby SDK sampleapp and they hit repeated 401s during streaming after token rotate. opened a tiny PR with a proposed sample fix and a note in README 
Priya: link?
Ravi: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/332 — gist: add token_provider callback support, reconnect-on-401 behavior for streaming clients, and a minimal spec that simulates a rotated token
Eve: nice. Is the reconnect strategy conservative? We should avoid double-submitting user events when resuming a stream
Ravi: yes, the sampleapp now stores last_event_id and resumes from that id after a single reconnect; we explicitly recommend idempotent event semantics in the README paragraph
Priya: can you paste the sample snippet here?
Ravi: sure:
```ruby
# sample token provider + resume semantics\class MyTokenProvider
  def initialize
    @token = OAuth.fetch
  end
  def token
    refresh_if_needed
    @token
  end
  def refresh_if_needed
    @token = OAuth.refresh! if token_expired?
  end
end
client = Redwood::Client.new(token_provider: MyTokenProvider.new)
# stream loop pseudo:
stream.each do |evt|
  process(evt) if seen_before?(evt.id) == false
end
```
Eve: good. For the test, did you stub the HTTP client so it returns 401 once then 200? We prefer deterministic retries in CI
Ravi: yes test/stream_retry_spec.rb stubs the HTTP adapter: 401 on first request, then 200 and asserts token_provider was called and that we resumed using last_event_id
CI-Bot: build #901 queued
Priya: tiny nit: README wording says "reconnect once" but code allows one retry per request. Maybe clarify: "on receiving 401, attempt token refresh and retry the request once; if still 401, surface error to the app"
Ravi: updated README and test assertion to reflect that wording
Eve: lgtm, also add a short note to troubleshooting that some identity providers return 403 on expired tokens instead of 401 — good to call that out
Ravi: added quick note and a link to the support doc. Will squash and merge after CI
